candidates.title: Prepare recovery checks for agent runs

demandEvidence.chore: Write checkpointers, recovery logic, and handle idempotency for agent runs.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A draft recovery checklist for one fictional agent workflow failure, including a checkpoint and safe retry decision.
inputs: A fictional agent workflow with three named steps
A simulated failure point and stored checkpoint
A proposed retry action and side-effect note
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a fictional failed agent run for review.
steps: List the workflow steps and possible side effects.
Mark where a checkpoint would preserve progress.
Draft a recovery action for the simulated failure.
Flag retries that could repeat an external side effect.
Ask a person to approve any real recovery design.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a sample workflow, verify every proposed retry names a checkpoint and flags any repeated side effect for human review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer must define real checkpoints, persistence, idempotency rules, and approve any action on production agents.
unverified: No supplied reference supports checkpointing, recovery execution, or idempotency controls.
The post gives no agent framework, recurrence, or tested recovery result.

ease.reason: A checklist can be drafted from fictional steps, but the post supplies no implementation reference for agent recovery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams operating AI agents may pay for recovery help; this discussion establishes a chore, not purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week paper prototype is possible, but safe recovery behavior and framework-specific inputs are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: The proposal only drafts checks; a developer must design and authorize every real recovery action.

evidence.reason: The fresh request names checkpointers, recovery logic, and idempotency, but gives no workflow details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: concrete chore assessed as a draft checklist; implementation and buyer support are absent.

experimentPlan.output: A draft index and plain-language note for one operator-supplied schematic page.

Operator-supplied component labels
A short list of documentation questions
experimentPlan.trigger: An engineer supplies one schematic page and asks for a documentation index.
steps: Record the labels and page references supplied by the operator.
Group related labels into a draft index.
Draft short navigation notes using only supplied descriptions.
Mark unclear or missing connections instead of guessing.
Have an electrical engineer verify every note against the drawing.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare the draft index with a fictional page whose labels and known links are supplied in advance; flag any invented label or connection.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An electrical engineer must supply readable design material and verify all component relationships; the draft is not design advice.
unverified: No supplied reference supports schematic OCR, circuit interpretation, or PDF annotation.
The source excerpt does not describe input formats, recurring volume, or evaluation results.

ease.reason: A text-only index can be drafted from operator notes, but no supplied reference supports schematic parsing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: electrical design consultancies may pay for documentation help; the maker excerpt does not establish buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week manual-input prototype is scopeable, while image reading and circuit accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed notes need an engineer to supply context and verify each connection.

evidence.reason: The excerpt identifies documentation and navigation as goals but supplies no detailed repeated workflow or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the task is stated, but useful design interpretation and implementation are unsupported.

candidates.title: Consolidate scattered trip details

demandEvidence.chore: Gather trip details scattered across spreadsheets, airline apps, old inboxes, and a photo library.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: My trips were scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library, so I built Trvlrr to hold all of it.

experimentPlan.output: A draft trip summary that groups operator-supplied travel details into one itinerary record.
inputs: Fictional trip dates and destination
Operator-supplied booking text copied from a sample email
A sample flight or lodging note
A list of missing fields to check
experimentPlan.trigger: A traveler pastes a small set of fictional trip notes into a manual intake form.
steps: Separate each supplied note by trip.
Extract dates, locations, and booking references into draft fields.
Mark conflicting or missing details for review.
Assemble one itinerary summary per trip.
Ask a person to verify the summary against original records.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use a fictional set of notes with known dates and locations; confirm every output field matches a supplied note and conflicts are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A traveler must provide and verify records; the prototype should use fictional data and must not access personal inboxes or accounts.
unverified: No supplied reference supports email, airline, spreadsheet, or photo-library integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: frequent travelers may pay for trip organization; this maker post reports no external buyer demand.

evidence.reason: The author directly describes scattered trip records and a tool to hold them together, without usage or demand details.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a synthetic organizer can be scoped, but integrations, usage evidence, and buyers are unverified.

An operator-supplied list of names to replace with placeholders
A short summary format chosen by the operator

candidates.title: Plan recovery for deleted workflows

demandEvidence.chore: Restore deleted production workflows to resume a business operation.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Several of them were active production workflows (our customer WhatsApp chatbot), so our business is currently down.

experimentPlan.output: A draft restoration checklist that maps an operator supplied workflow export inventory to a human reviewed recovery order.
inputs: A fictional workflow inventory with non-sensitive labels
Operator supplied sanitized workflow exports
A fictional dependency list and restore constraints
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a sanitized export inventory after a simulated workflow deletion.
steps: List each supplied workflow label and its stated dependency.
Mark missing exports or dependencies as unresolved.
Draft a proposed restore order from the supplied dependency list.
Create a verification checklist for each restored workflow using fictional test cases.
Require the operator to authorize and perform any real restoration.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fictional inventory with a known dependency order, confirm the checklist includes each supplied workflow once, respects the stated order, and flags missing exports without inventing recovery steps.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A system owner must provide authorized exports, verify dependencies, restore workflows, check credentials separately, and approve any production changes; this proposal does not access or restore an account.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports workflow backup, restoration, or n8n Cloud access.
The retained spans describe a deletion and outage but do not establish export availability, dependencies, or recoverability.
This is a single urgent incident report and does not establish recurrence or buyer willingness to pay.

ease.reason: A checklist can be tested with fictional inventories, but no supplied reference supports restoration or platform access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small firms reliant on workflow automations may pay for recovery planning; the post establishes no purchase intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week runbook mock is scopeable, but real recovery depends on authorized exports and verified dependencies.

autonomy.reason: The draft can organize supplied recovery details, while a system owner must restore and verify every production workflow.

evidence.reason: The retained span establishes deleted active production workflows and a business outage, but not backups, recovery steps, or recurrence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a fictional-data recovery checklist is assessable, but no restoration capability, export availability, or buyer evidence is supplied.
